::: {.why}
The sequence you sketched last night is the whole design; everything else in the engine is bookkeeping, and a wrong sequence is a leak that no test outside the engine will find.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Implement a session-level event loop where the sequence of read, decide, order, fill and mark is fixed and explicit.
- Show that the engine cannot compute a signal from data timestamped after the decision point, by construction rather than by convention.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [40 min]{.task-min} Write qlib/backtest/engine.py: for each session, present the strategy with a read-only view of the store as of the decision timestamp, collect orders, pass them to a fill model, apply fills to a portfolio, then mark to market at the close. The strategy never receives the store itself, only the as-of view, which is what makes the leak impossible rather than unlikely.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [20 min]{.task-min} Port the trend follower to it and reconcile against the vectorised version on a period where the two should agree. Any difference is either an assumption you now represent correctly or a bug, and separating those two is the exercise.
:::
:::

## The running strategy

::: {.project}
qlib/backtest/engine.py is the event loop the rest of the year runs on. The strategy sees an as-of view rather than the store, so look-ahead is prevented by the interface rather than by care.
:::
